review: 701.60d skip: the reason was false. Frantic Scapegoat's 'you may suspect one of the other creatures. If you do, Frantic Scapegoat is no longer suspected' depends on whether the suspect happened, so an already suspected target changes the outcome; removed the skip and added scenario 701.60d-1 (Frantic Scapegoat with Barbed Servitor, trigger order as the delta).

701.60b-1: the copy_scapegoat variant was labelled does_not_fire, but the Clone ends suspected by its own copied enters trigger, not by the rule failing; relabelled it other. Suspected is never copied, so the rule has no does_not_fire branch.
triage: rules/triage/701.60.jsonl was missing, so validate never checked this file; wrote it.

scenarios.title: An already suspected creature can't become suspected again

setup.notes: Frantic Scapegoat entered on an earlier turn and is suspected (menace, cannot block).

decisions: A casts Barbed Servitor, tapping the four Swamps.

Both players pass; Barbed Servitor resolves and enters. Two of A's abilities trigger: Barbed Servitor's 'When this enters, suspect it' and Frantic Scapegoat's 'Whenever one or more other creatures you control enter'.
A puts Frantic Scapegoat's trigger on the stack first and Barbed Servitor's trigger on top of it.
Both players pass; Barbed Servitor's trigger resolves and suspects Barbed Servitor.
Both players pass; Frantic Scapegoat's trigger resolves and A chooses to suspect Barbed Servitor.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Barbed Servitor is already suspected and does not become suspected again, so A did not suspect a creature. Frantic Scapegoat stays suspected (menace, cannot block) and Barbed Servitor is suspected (menace, cannot block).

variants.label: scapegoat_trigger_first
variants.delta: A puts Barbed Servitor's trigger on the stack first and Frantic Scapegoat's trigger on top of it, so Frantic Scapegoat's trigger resolves first.
variants.expected: Frantic Scapegoat's trigger suspects Barbed Servitor, which was not yet suspected, and Frantic Scapegoat is no longer suspected (no menace, can block). Barbed Servitor's own trigger then does nothing; Barbed Servitor is suspected (menace, cannot block).

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge's Card.setSuspected returns true for a card that is already suspected, so Frantic Scapegoat's RememberAltered may record Barbed Servitor and end Frantic Scapegoat's suspicion in the base variant too; Forge is expected to diverge from the rules here.

scenarios.title: A suspected creature stops being suspected when an ability says so

setup.notes: Frantic Scapegoat entered on an earlier turn and is suspected (menace, cannot block). It is not summoning sick.

decisions: A casts Grizzly Bears, tapping both Forests.
Both players pass; Grizzly Bears resolves and enters.
Frantic Scapegoat's trigger goes on the stack; both players pass.
On resolution A chooses to suspect Grizzly Bears.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears becomes suspected (menace, cannot block). Frantic Scapegoat is no longer suspected: it has no menace and can block.

variants.label: declined
variants.delta: On resolution A chooses not to suspect Grizzly Bears.
variants.expected: Frantic Scapegoat remains suspected (menace, cannot block) and Grizzly Bears is not suspected (no menace, can block).

scenarios.forge_notes: Frantic Scapegoat's second trigger uses CheckSVar on its own suspected status, so the setup requires the Scapegoat to be suspected when Grizzly Bears enters.

scenarios.title: A creature stays suspected until it leaves the battlefield

setup.notes: Caught Red-Handed gains control of the target creature until end of turn and suspects it. Cloudshift is held in every variant and cast only in one.

decisions: A casts Caught Red-Handed targeting B's Grizzly Bears, tapping the five Mountains.
Both players pass; Caught Red-Handed resolves: A gains control of Grizzly Bears until end of turn, untaps it, it gains haste, and it becomes suspected.
A does not cast Cloudshift; A attacks with nothing and passes through the turn to A's cleanup step.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: At A's cleanup step control returns to B. Grizzly Bears never left the battlefield, so it is still suspected: B's Grizzly Bears has menace and cannot block.

variants.label: flickered
variants.delta: After Caught Red-Handed resolves, A casts Cloudshift targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping Plains.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is exiled and returns to the battlefield as a new object under A's control. It is not suspected: no menace and it can block. The until-end-of-turn control effect no longer applies to it, so it stays under A's control after the turn ends.

scenarios.forge_notes: Cloudshift returns the card under its caster's control; the Caught Red-Handed control effect belongs to the old object.

scenarios.title: Suspected is not copiable

setup.notes: B's Grizzly Bears is suspected (menace, cannot block), put there on an earlier turn by a suspecting effect that is no longer on the stack.

decisions: A casts Clone, tapping all four Islands.
Both players pass; Clone resolves and enters.
A chooses to have Clone enter as a copy of B's Grizzly Bears.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Clone enters as a 2/2 Grizzly Bears that is not suspected: no menace and it can block. B's original Grizzly Bears is still suspected.

variants.label: copy_scapegoat
variants.delta: B's creature is a suspected Frantic Scapegoat instead of a suspected Grizzly Bears.
variants.expected: Clone enters as a Frantic Scapegoat and its copied enters trigger resolves, suspecting the Clone: it ends suspected because of its own ability, not because the designation was copied. B's original Frantic Scapegoat is still suspected.

scenarios.forge_notes: In the copy_scapegoat variant B's Frantic Scapegoat is on the battlefield instead of B's Grizzly Bears, and its other-creatures-enter trigger belongs to B, so A's Clone does not trigger it.

scenarios.title: A suspected creature can't block

setup.notes: A's Grizzly Bears is attacking B. B's Repeat Offender is untapped and suspected in the base variant (B activated its ability on an earlier turn).

decisions: A attacked B with Grizzly Bears and it is the declare blockers step: B considers blocking Grizzly Bears with Repeat Offender.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Repeat Offender is not a legal blocker for Grizzly Bears: it is suspected and cannot block.

variants.label: not_suspected
variants.expected: Repeat Offender is a legal blocker for Grizzly Bears.

scenarios.forge_notes: Repeat Offender is used because its suspected status is easy to reach by one of its own activations.

scenarios.title: A suspected creature has menace

setup.notes: A's Repeat Offender is attacking B and is suspected (A activated its ability on an earlier turn). Both of B's Grizzly Bears are untapped.

decisions: A attacked B with Repeat Offender and it is the declare blockers step.
B declares one Grizzly Bears as the only blocker of Repeat Offender.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: The block is illegal: a suspected creature has menace and cannot be blocked except by two or more creatures.

variants.label: two_blockers
variants.delta: B declares both Grizzly Bears as blockers of Repeat Offender.
variants.expected: The block is legal: Repeat Offender is blocked by two creatures.
